title: Personal jurisdiction over out-of-state defendants
question: When can a court reach a defendant who is not from the forum?

steps.note: Power runs with territory: a state binds people and property inside its borders, and little else.
Implied consent: driving on state roads appoints a state officer as agent for service.
Minimum contacts and “fair play and substantial justice” replace physical power.
One insurance contract with a resident is enough when the claim arises from it.
Purposeful availment: the plaintiff’s unilateral moves do not create the defendant’s contacts.
Shoe governs quasi in rem too; property in the forum is a contact, not a substitute for contacts.
Foreseeability that a car might be driven anywhere is not enough; the defendant must reach the forum.
Intentional torts aimed at the forum: the effects test.
A contract plus a course of dealing can be a contact; two steps, contacts then fairness factors.
Stream of commerce splits four to four; fairness factors alone can defeat jurisdiction.
Tag jurisdiction survives: service on a visitor in the forum is enough.
General jurisdiction only where the corporation is “at home”.
Stream of commerce again, no majority: the plurality wants targeting of the forum.
“At home” means incorporation or principal place of business, save an exceptional case.
Contacts with the forum itself, not with a plaintiff who lives there.
Each plaintiff’s claim must arise from the defendant’s forum contacts.
“Relate to” needs no strict causation when the defendant cultivates the forum market.
Registration-based consent is a separate road, under Pennsylvania Fire.
